400.description: Invalid argument - The client specified an invalid argument

401.description: Unauthenticated - The request does not have valid authentication credentials

403.description: Permission denied - The caller does not have permission to execute the specified operation

404.description: Not found - Some requested entity was not found

408.description: Deadline exceeded - The deadline expired before the operation could complete

412.description: Failed precondition - Operation was rejected because the system is not in required state

413.description: Out of range - Operation was attempted past the valid range

429.description: Resource exhausted - Some resource has been exhausted (rate limiting)

431.description: Request header fields too large - Request metadata was too large

AnthropicBeta.description:
Beta names you can send in the `anthropic-beta` header.

See [Beta headers](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta-headers) for how to send them and where to find the name a feature needs.

BetaManagedAgentsMemoryView.description:
Whether a `memory` or `memory_version` in the response includes its `content`. Defaults to `full` on retrieve operations and to `basic` on list, create, and update operations.

With `full`, list operations return at most 20 items per page.

BetaManagedAgentsMemory.description:
A text document at a path inside a memory store.

`content` is `null` when the response uses `view=basic`. `content_size_bytes` and `content_sha256` are always set, so you can detect changes without fetching the content. To retrieve, update, or delete a memory, pass its ID, which stays the same when its path changes.

See the [memory guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#view-and-edit-memories) to learn more about working with memories.

content.description:
The memory's UTF-8 text content, or `null` when the response uses `view=basic`.

The maximum size is 100 kB (102,400 bytes).

content_sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 digest of the UTF-8 `content` bytes (64 characters). The server applies no normalization, so clients can compute the same hash locally for staleness checks and as the value for a `content_sha256` precondition on update. Always populated, regardless of `view`.

content_size_bytes.description: The size of the memory's `content` in UTF-8 bytes. It is set regardless of `view`.

created_at.description: When this memory was created, in RFC 3339 format.

id.description:
The unique ID of the memory (`mem_...`). It stays the same when the memory's path changes.

To retrieve, update, or delete the memory, pass this ID.

memory_store_id.description: ID of the memory store this memory belongs to (a `memstore_...` value).

memory_version_id.description:
The ID of the memory version that holds the memory's current content (`memver_...`).

Memory versions don't have a flag that marks the latest one. Compare their IDs with this field instead.

See the [memory guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#audit-memory-changes) to learn more about memory versions.

path.description: Hierarchical path of the memory within the store, e.g. `/projects/foo/notes.md`. Always starts with `/`. Paths are case-sensitive and unique within a store. Maximum 1,024 bytes.

updated_at.description:
When the memory was last changed, in RFC 3339.

To find out who made the change, look at `created_by` on the memory version that `memory_version_id` references.

BetaManagedAgentsMemoryPreconditionFaile.description:
The error returned with HTTP status 409 when a request's precondition doesn't hold for the memory's current state, such as `precondition` on an update or `expected_content_sha256` on a delete.

The error doesn't include the memory's current state. Retrieve the memory to see its current content and `content_sha256` before you retry.

See the [memory guide](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/memory#safe-content-edits-optimistic-concurrency) to learn more about safe content edits with content hash preconditions.

BetaManagedAgentsMemoryPathConflictError.description:
The error returned with HTTP status 409 when you create or rename a memory and the path you give is already used by another memory or overlaps another memory's path.

Two paths overlap when one is an ancestor of the other, such as `/notes` and `/notes/todo.md`. To free the path, rename or delete the memory that `conflicting_memory_id` references, then retry. To change that memory instead of creating a new one, update it.

To handle the error in code, use `conflicting_path` and `conflicting_memory_id` instead of `message`.

conflicting_memory_id.description:
The ID of the memory that blocked the write (`mem_...`), or an empty string if that memory can't be identified.

Retry the request when it is empty.

conflicting_path.description: The path that blocked the write: the requested path, or the path of a memory that is an ancestor or descendant of it.
